Play action off run looks is the most likely way to attack HOU's light-to-average boxes, and screens are a lower-priority option.

report.title: IND at HOU Week 11 Scouting Report
report.summary: Houston leans on the pass on early downs but runs more when the distance is short, and it attacks intermediate more than deep. Its pressure is mostly four-man, so quick game and max protection belong in the plan. Indiana's clearest openings are against the run on early downs and in the kicking and return game. Injuries on both lines make pass protection the main concern.

Houston uses pre-snap motion on 55.4% of plays [oc14] and play action on 19.4% of dropbacks [oc15], so Indiana's safeties must stay disciplined against motion and play fakes. Its explosive pass play rate is 10.0% [oc18], and its average depth of target is 9.7 yards [oc21] over 319 pass attempts [oc22], so shots come more from intermediate throws than deep ones. Targets lean toward Collins at 18.1% [oc23], and Marks takes 53.2% of designed rushes [oc26]. Houston converts 38.6% of third-down plays [oc28] over 114 plays [oc29], ranked 17th [oc30].

sections.heading: Opponent defense
sections.body: Houston sends extra rushers on 24.6% of dropbacks [dc1] over 358 plays [dc2], ranked 25th [dc3], and averages 4.3 pass rushers per dropback [dc4]. Its pressure proxy of 16.8% [dc5] compares with 17.8% [dc6] allowed by Indiana, so plan for a mostly four-man rush with occasional five-man pressure. Against the run Houston allows a 42.7% success rate [dc7] on 218 run plays [dc8], with 6.9 defenders in the box [dc10]. Explosive plays come on 10.1% of pass plays [dc12], so shot plays are available if Indiana gets a clean look. On third-down plays Houston allows a 40.0% conversion rate [dc14] on 120 plays [dc15], ranked 17th [dc16], and in the red zone it allows touchdowns on 68.0% of drives [dc17], though that is a small sample of 25 drives [dc18]. Indiana's play action ranks 5th [dc21] and its RPOs 15th [dc22], so play action off run looks is the most likely way to attack Houston's light-to-average boxes.

sections.heading: Special teams
sections.body: Houston's only kicker this season is K. Fairbairn, who has made 19 [kc3] of 20 [kc2] field goal tries, a 95.0% [kc1] make rate, and 87.5% [kc4] of 50-plus tries over 8 [kc5] attempts. Treat his range as real, so do not gift Houston short fields. Houston's punting is average, with 41.4 [kc6] net yards per punt on 39 [kc7] punts, and only 28.2% [kc8] of punts pin opponents inside the 20. Kickoffs rarely produce touchbacks, at 17.6% [kc9] on 51 [kc10] kickoffs. Houston's punt returns are weak at 5.6 [kc13] yards on 25 [kc14] returns, so punting to that returner carries little risk. Overall special-teams EPA is -0.02 [kc15] over 261 [kc16] plays, ranking 20th [kc17], so Indiana has a real opening in the third phase.

sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: Houston's latest report lists DE Danielle Hunter as Out [ic1] with a 75.6% snap share [ic2] over 8 [ic3] games, so expect more edge rotation. DE Will Anderson Jr. is Questionable [ic4] with a 77.2% snap share [ic5] over 9 [ic6] games, so if he sits, edge pressure drops sharply. RB David Montgomery is Questionable [ic7] and has taken 25.9% of team rushes [ic8], so backups absorb those carries. On Indiana's side, tackle Jalen Travis is Out [ic13] with a 92.8% snap share [ic14] over 9 [ic15] games, so pass protection depth gets tested. DT Jerry Tillery and TE Mo Alie-Cox are also Out, leaving Indiana's front and tight end depth thin.

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: Houston's downfield passing is the first concern: its explosive pass play rate is 10.0% [mc1], and Indiana allows explosive passes on 10.5% [mc2] over 334 pass plays [mc3]. Keep a deep safety over the top on early downs and track Collins, who draws 18.1% [mc4] of targets. Pass protection without Jalen Travis, who averaged 92.8% [mc5] of snaps per game, is the second concern. Indiana has allowed a 17.8% [mc6] pressure proxy, but Houston blitzes on only 24.6% [mc7] of dropbacks, so quick game and max protection both belong in the plan. Third, commit to the run on early downs: Houston allows a 42.7% [mc8] run success rate with 6.9 [mc9] defenders in the box, and throws on only 41.0% [mc10] of short-yardage plays. Finally, Fairbairn has made 95.0% [mc13] of field goals on 20 [mc14] attempts, so avoid short fields, and punt to a returner averaging 5.6 [mc16] yards on punt returns.
